note: doc 06 section 2.6. An archetype is finer than a role: a role says how a player plays the position, an archetype says which job he does inside a unit and what the unit then needs around him. Attached to a slot family, not a position code, because the eight in a 4-3-3 and the eight in a 3-5-2 are different jobs. duties_json is a closed seven-word vocabulary and is what the unit_balance_rules checker runs on. Duty definitions used consistently across every row below: tempo (decides how fast the ball circulates), progression (moves the ball past an opponent line, by pass or by carry, including beating a man), rest_defence (holds the space that protects the counter), width (occupies the touchline and holds the opposing fullback out), pin (occupies the last defensive line and holds the centre backs deep), box_threat (arrives in the opposition penalty area to finish), press_trigger (starts the press or steps out of the line to meet the ball). width and pin are deliberately separated: one stretches the pitch sideways, the other stretches it in depth.

items.name: Sweeper Keeper
items.definition: Defends the space between himself and a high defensive line, and acts as the spare man when the press comes.
items.needs_around_it: A back line willing to defend high, because a sweeper keeper behind a deep block has nothing to sweep.
items.exemplar_note: Manuel Neuer, Marc-Andre ter Stegen. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Distributing Keeper
items.definition: Starts the possession as an extra passer and breaks the first line with his feet, without necessarily defending high space.
items.needs_around_it: Centre backs who split wide and a six who shows for the return, or he has nobody to pass to.
items.exemplar_note: Ederson, Alisson. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Line Keeper
items.definition: Holds his line, commands his box on crosses, and distributes long rather than short.
items.needs_around_it: A target man or a genuine second-ball unit, because his first option is length, not a short pass.
items.exemplar_note: Petr Cech, Gianluigi Buffon. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Stopper
items.definition: Front-foot centre back who steps out of the line to kill the attack at its source and wins his duel early.
items.needs_around_it: A covering partner who holds the line behind him, or the space he vacates is the space they run into.
items.exemplar_note: Sergio Ramos, Cristian Romero. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Coverer
items.definition: Reads the pass before it is played, defends the space behind his partner, and wins the footrace to balls in behind.
items.needs_around_it: A partner who steps, because two coverers means nobody ever meets the ball in front of the line.
items.exemplar_note: Raphael Varane, Ruben Dias. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Ball-Playing Centre Back
items.definition: Breaks the first line from a standing start, either with the vertical pass into midfield or the diagonal that switches the attack.
items.needs_around_it: A six who moves to open the passing lane, otherwise the pass he is picked for never has a target.
items.exemplar_note: Gerard Pique, Virgil van Dijk. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Stepping Pivot
items.definition: Steps out of the back line into midfield in possession to make the pivot a two, then drops back as the ball turns over.
items.needs_around_it: A partner and a fullback who cover the space he leaves, and a coach who accepts a back three in possession.
items.exemplar_note: John Stones (Manchester City, as the centre back who becomes a midfielder). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Stepping Wide Centre Back
items.definition: The outside centre back in a back three who follows his man out of the line into the channel and into midfield.
items.needs_around_it: A central centre back who slides across behind him, or the channel he leaves is the pass they are looking for.
items.exemplar_note: Antonio Ruediger (in a back three), Kim Min-jae. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Channel Defender
items.definition: The outside centre back who holds the line, defends the channel between himself and the wingback, and rarely leaves the three.
items.needs_around_it: A wingback who tracks back, because he will not follow the runner past halfway himself.
items.exemplar_note: Cesar Azpilicueta (as the right of a back three). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Carrying Wide Centre Back
items.definition: Carries the ball out of the back three into the space a retreating winger leaves, and passes forward from midfield height.
items.needs_around_it: A wingback high enough to pin the winger, so the ten metres in front of him are actually empty.
items.exemplar_note: Alessandro Bastoni, Aymeric Laporte. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Overlapping Centre Back
items.definition: Goes beyond the wingback on the outside, turning the back three into a two and making an extra man in the wide third.
items.needs_around_it: A six who drops into the back line as he leaves, or the overlap costs the rest defence a body.
items.exemplar_note: Chris Basham and Jack O'Connell (Sheffield United's overlapping centre backs). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Overlapping Fullback
items.definition: Runs outside the winger to the byline and delivers, so the width in the final third comes from the back line.
items.needs_around_it: A winger who comes inside and takes his marker with him, plus a midfielder who covers the flank on the turnover.
items.exemplar_note: Dani Alves, Andrew Robertson. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Inverted Fullback
items.definition: Steps inside into the pivot in possession to overload the middle and protect the counter before the ball is lost.
items.needs_around_it: A winger or a wide-rotating eight who holds the touchline, because he takes the width away when he steps in.
items.exemplar_note: Philipp Lahm (under Guardiola), Joao Cancelo. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Underlapping Fullback
items.definition: Comes inside and forward into the half-space beyond the midfield line, rather than dropping into the pivot behind it.
items.needs_around_it: A winger holding the touchline and a six who screens, because his run leaves the flank behind him empty.
items.exemplar_note: Trent Alexander-Arnold (in the high inside role), Alejandro Grimaldo. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Defensive Fullback
items.definition: Defends his one-versus-one first, stays in the back four, and offers the short sideways pass rather than the overlap.
items.needs_around_it: A winger who can hold the width alone, because no width will ever arrive from behind him.
items.exemplar_note: Gary Neville, Nathaniel Clyne. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Attacking Wingback
items.definition: Runs the whole touchline, supplies the width on his side by himself, and reaches the byline in every settled attack.
items.needs_around_it: A back three that stays as a three, and a wide forward who plays inside him rather than on top of him.
items.exemplar_note: Achraf Hakimi, Marcos Alonso (as a left wingback). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Defensive Wingback
items.definition: Plays as the fifth defender first and joins the attack only once the ball is settled on his side of the pitch.
items.needs_around_it: A wide forward or an eight who takes the high touchline, since he arrives late or not at all.
items.exemplar_note: Victor Moses (Chelsea 2016/17). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Inverted Wingback
items.definition: Tucks into midfield in possession to build a box in the middle, leaving the touchline to the wide forward ahead of him.
items.needs_around_it: A wide forward who genuinely stays on the touchline, or the shape has a box in the middle and nothing outside it.

items.name: Metronome
items.definition: Sits in front of the back line, is always available for the return pass, and sets the speed the whole team plays at.
items.needs_around_it: At least one eight who breaks forward, because he will circulate all afternoon and never break a line himself.
items.exemplar_note: Sergio Busquets, Jorginho. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Deep Line Breaker
items.definition: Plays from the metronome's position but looks first for the pass that goes past a line rather than around it.
items.needs_around_it: A ball winner or a destroyer near him, because his eyes are upfield and his first thought is not the counter.
items.exemplar_note: Andrea Pirlo, Toni Kroos. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Destroyer
items.definition: Screens the back line, hunts the ball in the middle third, and ends their attack before it reaches the last line.
items.needs_around_it: Someone alongside who can pass, because he wins the ball and then needs an outlet within two seconds.
items.exemplar_note: Claude Makelele, N'Golo Kante. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Carrying Six
items.definition: Beats the first press by driving out of the pivot with the ball instead of passing around it.
items.needs_around_it: Two forward options ahead of the carry, or he drives into traffic and loses it in the worst area of the pitch.
items.exemplar_note: Declan Rice, Fernandinho. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Shuttler
items.definition: The forward-going half of a double pivot: covers ground box to box and arrives in the opposition area from deep.
items.needs_around_it: A controller beside him who stays, because the pivot becomes a one every time he goes.
items.exemplar_note: Patrick Vieira, Steven Gerrard. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Half-Space Creator
items.definition: Receives between their midfield and back line in the half-space and plays the pass that beats the last line.
items.needs_around_it: A six who holds, and a winger who pins the fullback so the half-space stays open.
items.exemplar_note: David Silva, Kevin De Bruyne. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Box Crasher
items.definition: Arrives late and unmarked at the far post or the penalty spot, the third-man finisher of the midfield.
items.needs_around_it: Someone else holding the middle, because he will not be there when the ball turns over.
items.exemplar_note: Frank Lampard, Arturo Vidal. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Line-Breaking Carrier
items.definition: Breaks the line by driving through it rather than passing through it.
items.needs_around_it: Space to run into, so pair him with players who pin the last line rather than drop off it.
items.exemplar_note: Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Ball Winner
items.definition: The counterpress trigger of the midfield: wins the ball back in the five seconds after we lose it.
items.needs_around_it: A creator alongside, or the trio has no forward pass.
items.exemplar_note: Gennaro Gattuso, Javier Mascherano. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Deep Rotator
items.definition: Drops beside the six to make a temporary double pivot, then leaves once the line is broken.
items.needs_around_it: A partner who does the opposite, otherwise both drop and nobody occupies the space between the lines.
items.exemplar_note: Thiago Alcantara, Ilkay Gundogan. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Wide Rotator
items.definition: Takes the touchline when the fullback inverts, so the width never disappears.
items.needs_around_it: An inverting fullback, because without one this archetype is just a bad winger.
items.exemplar_note: Bernardo Silva (Manchester City, on the side Cancelo inverted from). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Between the Lines Ten
items.definition: Receives on the half-turn between their midfield and back line, then plays the pass that unlocks the last line.
items.needs_around_it: A nine who holds the last line, because the space he wants only exists while the centre backs are pinned.
items.exemplar_note: Mesut Ozil, Juan Roman Riquelme. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Shadow Striker
items.definition: Plays off the nine and attacks the box himself, a second forward wearing a midfield number.
items.needs_around_it: A nine who occupies both centre backs, or he arrives in a box that is already full.
items.exemplar_note: Dele Alli (Tottenham under Pochettino). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Pressing Ten
items.definition: The first defender of a mid block: screens their pivot in the rest shape and springs the trap when the ball goes wide.
items.needs_around_it: Two forwards or wingers who press the same side with him, because the trigger only works if the trap closes.

items.name: Touchline Winger
items.definition: Stays on the chalk until the ball arrives, then attacks the fullback one versus one.
items.needs_around_it: A fullback who stays inside or behind him, because two players on the same touchline is one player wasted.
items.exemplar_note: Jeremy Doku, Antonio Valencia. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Inside Forward
items.definition: Starts wide, comes inside onto his stronger foot, and finishes from the half-space.
items.needs_around_it: A fullback who overlaps outside him, or the flank he leaves is simply empty.
items.exemplar_note: Arjen Robben, Mohamed Salah. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Channel Runner
items.definition: Attacks the space between the centre back and the fullback the moment the ball can be played forward.
items.needs_around_it: A midfielder who can pick the pass before the run dies, because timing without service is just running.
items.exemplar_note: Kylian Mbappe, Thierry Henry (from the left). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Raumdeuter
items.definition: Holds no width and beats nobody, but arrives unmarked in the box because he read the space earlier than the defender.
items.needs_around_it: A team-mate supplying width on his side, since he will not provide any of it himself.
items.exemplar_note: Thomas Muller (the archetype takes its name from his own description of the job). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Pressing Winger
items.definition: Sets the press from the front with the curved run that locks the ball onto one side of the pitch.
items.needs_around_it: A fullback and an eight who step up with him, because a solo press is only a warning to the opponent.
items.exemplar_note: Sadio Mane (Liverpool under Klopp). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Target Man
items.definition: Holds the ball with his back to goal, wins the first contact, and brings the runners around him into the game.
items.needs_around_it: Runners who go past him the instant he wins the header, or the second ball is theirs every time.
items.exemplar_note: Didier Drogba, Olivier Giroud. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Runner in Behind
items.definition: Plays on the shoulder and attacks the space behind the last line before the defence can drop into it.
items.needs_around_it: A passer who looks up early, because the run is made once and does not come back.
items.exemplar_note: Jamie Vardy, Erling Haaland. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: False Nine
items.definition: Leaves the last line and drops into midfield, asking the centre backs whether they follow him or let him turn.
items.needs_around_it: Wide forwards who attack the space he vacates, or the back four keeps its shape and simply gains a spare man.
items.exemplar_note: Lionel Messi (Barcelona under Guardiola), Cesc Fabregas (Spain 2012). Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Poacher
items.definition: Lives on the last shoulder inside the width of the box and does almost all of his work in the final six yards.
items.needs_around_it: A steady supply of cutbacks and low crosses, because he does not build the chance he finishes.
items.exemplar_note: Filippo Inzaghi, Ruud van Nistelrooy. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.

items.name: Pressing Forward
items.definition: Leads the press, sets the angle that shuts off the switch, and defends from the front for the full ninety minutes.
items.needs_around_it: A midfield that steps up with him, because a forward pressing alone only tells the opponent which way to play.
items.exemplar_note: Roberto Firmino, Gabriel Jesus. Not a licence: names are editorial reference points only.
